description: Vienna - Official .NET SDK for Captivate Chat API. Provides real-time WebSocket communication, HTTP messaging, file management, and multi-tenant support. Built with SOLID principles and full async/await support. Blue mode: the same calls talk to a Vienna Blue bot with a key for your app or a server key.
releaseNotes: v2.1.0: Blue mode. A key for your app from Vienna Blue's Channels page (vba_) talks to a Blue bot with the same calls, over HTTPS with no socket: each answer while it's written (OnDelta), the final answer with its sources and quick replies (OnAnswer), what the bot is doing (OnStep), StopAsync, and Resume; a dropped connection is read back, never sent again. Conversations by user (each user's secret in Storage or memory, UserSecret for one list on every device, ForgetUserAsync), metadata kept up to 4 KB, transcripts in 2.0's shapes; the signed-in customer and the details the bot's look-ups read; the bot's forms, look-ups and links (OnActionReceived, SendActionAsync); files through conversation.FileManager. A server key (vbk_) on your own server is server mode: GetConversation(id, userId), each user their own conversations and limits, nothing kept between requests, no key logged. Errors are CaptivateChatException (an HttpRequestException) in words users can see. New options: BlueUrl, HttpHandler, BlueReading, Storage, UserSecret, EventContext. Captivate's own keys work as in 2.0.0, with these fixes: Dispose stops the instance's conversations hearing its socket, and disposing an old instance leaves a newer one made for the same key and mode registered; debug mode no longer makes CreateConversationAsync fail, and debug logs and the manager's errors never show a key (a Captivate key is named by its last 4 characters, or by a short hash like #8XDtxiJ4 when it is under 16 characters, and a Blue app key by its kind and last 4 characters); a connect that times out closes its socket and clears its id, IsSocketActive() is true only once the socket has its id, and a CreateAsync that timed out disposes its instance; conversations send with the socket's current id after a reconnect; a dropped connection reconnects by itself (an aborted socket counts as dropped), and every send that finds the socket down reconnects first and then goes out with the new id, or throws InvalidOperationException with nothing sent when MaxReconnectAttempts tries fail; each ReconnectAsync makes up to MaxReconnectAttempts tries, each waiting for socket_connected; disconnecting sends its close and logs no error; messages over 8 KB arrive whole (over 4 MB one is dropped with a warning); ConnectAsync waits ConnectionTimeoutMs, not a fixed 10 s, and honours its cancellation token; with bot-first, CreateConversationAsync returns as soon as the conversation exists and sends the opener after, and the greeting is held for the first message listener. Captivate's keys now work in Blazor WebAssembly (the core HTTP client is a plain HttpClient in a browser, where SocketsHttpHandler throws Arg_PlatformNotSupported), CaptivateChatApi has DisposeAsync, and in a browser Dispose no longer waits on a thread for the close; DeleteUserConversationsAsync with a Captivate key sends the delete_user_conversations message captivate-chat-api sends, where it called an address the gateway doesn't have, and the overload that takes a list of ids throws NotSupportedException (the gateway can only delete all of a user's conversations). Behaviour changes: CreateConversationAsync no longer throws when the bot-first opener fails to send, the failure is logged and the conversation is returned; and after a lost connection a send waits for the reconnect and throws when it fails, where it used to return and lose its reply (README, Migrating to 2.1.0). Known limits with Captivate's gateway: every conversation on one connection hears every reply, deleting one conversation has no visible effect, and a bot-first greeting can be another conversation's reply when several open at once (README, Known limits). Samples in examples/BlueMode. No new dependency. v2.0.0: Aligned with TypeScript SDK v6.0. Added singleton pattern for CaptivateChatApi instances (automatic deduplication per API key/mode). Added IDisposable with Dispose() to close connections and remove from registry. Added conversation.FileManager (ConversationFileManager) for context-aware file operations. Added conversation.SetTimeToLiveAsync(days) for session TTL management. Added CaptivateChatManager.Dispose(apiKey) and DisposeAll() for multi-tenant cleanup. Fixed debug mode bug where OnWebSocketMessage bypassed SetDebugMode(false) and always wrote to console. Added GetInstance/HasInstance static helpers.
